references.text: The preceding verse describes those who feared the Lord's word and brought their servants and livestock inside, in contrast to those who did not heed the Lord's word in verse 21.
Proverbs warns of the consequences of failing to listen to wisdom and rejecting counsel, just as those who disregarded the Lord's word suffered under the hailstorm.
He who stiffens his neck when rebuked will suddenly be broken beyond healing—parallel to those who ignored the Lord's warning.
Isaiah speaks of Israel not knowing or understanding their Lord, similar to the Egyptians who did not set their hearts on the Lord's word.
Jeremiah describes a people with eyes but do not see, ears but do not hear—a spiritual blindness like that of those who ignored God's warning.
Jesus teaches about the servant who knew his master's will but did not act accordingly and will be severely punished—parallel to the consequences of ignoring the Lord's word.
Hebrews warns against neglecting salvation and failing to heed what has been spoken, noting that disobedience to the message delivered through angels received just punishment.
Illustrates how concrete resistance to God's word (Exodus) is a manifestation of the general breach of covenant (Psalms).
Psalm 78:37 explains the inner condition ('heart not firm') underlying the action in Exodus ('did not take the word to heart').
A clear parallel between Pharaoh's disobedience toward Moses and Jeremiah's time with disobedience toward the prophet.
Highlights the theological cause of disobedience: a 'hardened heart' that refuses to receive God's word.
Links disobedience ('did not hear') directly to a 'hardened heart' and the ensuing covenant curse in both texts.
Direct narrative connection: Pharaoh's hardened heart (7:13) leads to his failure to take the word to heart (9:21).
